newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebel chief's death certificate full of holes.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebel chief's death certificate full of holes.

text.p: The death certificate of rebel leader Nestor Cerpa, killed in a fiery raid on the Japanese ambassador's home, gave few clues on Friday about the man behind the siege that gripped world attention for four months.
The document, obtained by Reuters, listed Cerpa's marital status as unknown and left his exact age and occupation blank. He was "approximately 45," it said.

About the only thing it did say unequivocally about Cerpa was how he died: by bleeding to death from bullet wounds after Tuesday's assault on the residence by crack Peruvian troops who rescued all but one of 72 hostages held by the rebels.

Although Cerpa was believed to have spent recent years in hiding in Peru's central jungle region, his place of residence was listed as the upscale San Isidro district in Lima where he spent 126 days holed up inside the diplomatic mansion.
One section to be filled out in case of a violent death was also left blank.
Even the rebel leader's name was a puzzle -- recorded as Fortunato Cerpa Cartolini and not Nestor, as he was generally referred to.

The certificate also appeared to confuse the exact location of the guerrilla leader's death, indicating in one place it was the military hospital where his body was autopsied on Wednesday and not the residence.

Cerpa's body was shown sprawled face up on the stairs of the residence on Wednesday, a bullet wound in the head and a gash in his neck, in television footage of an inspection of the siege site by President Alberto Fujimori.
Fujimori said later that Cerpa was caught in a crossfire after being surprised playing indoor soccer with rebel comrades by troops who burst in through a tunnel under the building.
A separate document obtained by Reuters on Friday showed that Cerpa's family paid 230 soles ($87) for his burial at the Villa Maria cemetery in Lima.
One hostage, two army officers and all 14 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels died in Tuesday's internationally-acclaimed rescue mission.
